column1: # CodeBrix.LilyPort regression ratchet -- the BEST VERDICT EVER ACHIEVED
# per reference page. A run must meet or beat every row here; see
# ratchet.py for why this is a per-file floor and not a pass count.
# Advanced only by `ratchet.py update`, never by hand. A row that needs to
# come DOWN is a decision, not a fix: record why in the commit message.
# EMPTY ON PURPOSE, EPG0 (2026-08-04). The port cannot yet engrave a
# regression file end to end -- that arrives with EPG3 (output pipeline) and
# becomes meaningful at EPG4 (horizontal spacing), which is where notes stop
# sitting at x = 0. The machinery is committed FIRST so that the moment the
# first file produces a verdict, the floor exists to hold it: a ratchet
# retrofitted after the fact records whatever the port happened to be doing
# that day, which is how a suite ends up enshrining its own bugs.
